correctness.rationale: For A=F_q[t]/(t^n), p>n, the multiplier subgroup U has exponent p because its substitution matrices are unitriangular of nilpotency length at most n<p. The canonical commuting p-part and prime-to-p part of each automorphism permits a conjugate scalar multiplier σ_a (order d) and a unique centralizer parameter tuple (b_1,...,b_h), where h=floor((n−2)/d). The first nonzero b_j gives independent rows with leading coefficients kd*b_j, nonzero since 1≤kd<n<p; the resulting fixed ring is the scalar plus the upper truncated monomial ideal of dimension 1+j, and the trivial tuple gives 1+floor((n−1)/d). Counting first nonzero indices and Burnside yields exactly the stated conditional multiplicities and action-orbit sum. Boundary h=0, d=1 and coalescing dimensions are handled by adding multiplicities. Independently enumerated actual substitution matrices and fixed-space nullities at (5,3),(5,4),(7,4), recovering {1:10,2:9,3:1}, {1:50,2:45,3:4,4:1}, and {1:98,2:189,3:6,4:1}. The finite instances are checks, not proof for unbounded n/extension fields.
